Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7902 of 2023

Applicant :- Akhilesh Sonkar @ Kunnu
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Home, Lucknow And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Mohammad Imaran,Dildar Khan,Rehan Ahmad Siddiqui
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1 .  Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None turned up on behalf of the complainant despite notice.
2. In terms of the FIR, the allegations were leveled that the sister of the informant aged about 14 years when the applicant took her home.
It was also stated that when they tried to search her, it was informed that the sister was beaten and was thrown out from the house of the applicant.

Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim recorded that on the date of the incident, she was sleeping at home along with her father, when the applicant came at around 12 midnight and took her home, where the mother of the applicant was also present and mother of the Akhilesh Sonkar @ Kunnu vs State Of U.P. 1 applicant came along with the girl and informed the parents of the victim and thereafter, the mother of the victim took her back, however, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she made allegation with regard to the rape at the home of the applicant.
She also alleged that applicant was carrying a knife.

3. In the light of the said, the submission of the counsel for the applicant that there is a huge variance in the two statements of the victim, he places reliance on the statement of the neighbours,
who have stated that it was the mother of the applicant, who informed the mother of the victim that she had come to their home.
There is no recovery of knife from the applicant as alleged in the statement of the victim.
The medical on record does not corroborate the baseless allegations made in the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C.

The age of the victim based upon the report of the CMO is around 15-16 years, however, there is no document on record in terms of the provisions or the Rules framed under the Juvenile Justice Act to come to the conclusion with regard to the age of the victim.

The applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 06.02.2023.
4.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the huge variance in the statements under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., and the statement of the neighbours, who do not support the prosecution case coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 06.02.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Akhilesh Sonkar @ Kunnu be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 606 of 2022, under Sections 323, 363, 376, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Antu,
District Pratapgarh, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
